```{r, include = FALSE}
  collapse = TRUE,

```

```{r setup}
library(ggforestplotR)
library(ggplot2)
```


This guide covers fitted-model inputs, effect scales, model comparisons, and
derived subgroup effects. For appearance and layout, see
[Customize Forest Plots and Tables](ggforestplotR-plot-customization.html).

## Supported fitted models

Explicit conversion methods are available for the following classes. Their
tidiers must supply estimates and confidence limits.

| Model input | Required extraction packages | Output and scope |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `stats::lm()` (`lm`) | `broom` | Additive coefficients (Beta). |
| `stats::glm()` (`glm`) | `broom` | Scale follows family and link, as described below. |
| `survival::coxph()` (`coxph`) | `broom`, `survival` | Hazard ratios (HR). |
| `lme4` models (`merMod`) | `broom`, `broom.mixed`, `lme4` | Fixed effects; scale follows family and link. |
| `nlme::lme()` (`lme`) | `broom`, `broom.mixed`, `nlme` | Fixed-effect additive coefficients. |
| `glmmTMB::glmmTMB()` (`glmmTMB`) | `broom`, `broom.mixed`, `glmmTMB` | Conditional-model fixed effects; excludes zero-inflation and dispersion coefficients. |

Coefficient extraction and derived subgroup effects have different requirements.
Subgroup inference additionally uses `marginaleffects` and has the restrictions
described below. A `broom` tidier alone does not imply direct support for every
model class. For other inputs, use a coefficient table as described in
[Preparing Forest Data](ggforestplotR-data-helpers.html).

## Plot a fitted model

```{r direct-model}
fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp + qsec, data = mtcars)
ggforestplot(fit, term_labels = c("wt" = "Weight")) +
  add_forest_table()
```

## Inspect coefficients before plotting

If `broom` is available, the model-specific `as_forest_data()` method pulls
coefficient estimates and confidence limits from a fitted model. The method
also assigns model semantics such as `Beta`, `OR`, or `HR`.

```{r tidy-model}
fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp + qsec, data = mtcars)

model_ready <- as_forest_data(fit)
```

The returned object can be passed directly into `ggforestplot()`.

```{r helper-to-plot-model}
ggforestplot(model_ready)
```

`tidy_forest_model()` remains available as a compatibility wrapper and returns
the same `forest_data` object.


## Effect scales and confidence intervals

With `exponentiate = NULL`, binomial and quasibinomial logit models use odds
ratios, Cox models use hazard ratios, and log-link Poisson models use incidence
rate ratios. Binomial log-link models use risk ratios; identity-link binomial
models use risk differences. Other log-link families use a ratio label.
Linear models retain additive coefficients.

For fitted models, `exponentiate = FALSE` retains unexponentiated coefficients;
`TRUE` transforms coefficients and bounds. For data frames, `TRUE` instead
declares values that are **already ratios** and does not transform them.
Ratio plots default to a log10 axis with reference value 1.

Use `as_forest_data(fit, conf.level = 0.90)` to request a different confidence
level. Confidence intervals are required. Intercepts are omitted by default;
use `as_forest_data(fit, intercept = TRUE)` to retain them.

### Logistic regression

```{r logistic-model}
logit_fit <- glm(am ~ mpg + cyl, data = mtcars, family = binomial())
ggforestplot(logit_fit, striped_rows = TRUE) + add_forest_table()
```

### Survival analysis

```{r survival-model}
cox_fit <- survival::coxph(
  survival::Surv(time, status == 2) ~ ph.ecog + sex,
  data = survival::lung
)
ggforestplot(cox_fit, striped_rows = TRUE) + add_forest_table()
```

### Mixed models

```{r mixed-model}
mixed_fit <- lme4::lmer(
  Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject), data = lme4::sleepstudy
)
ggforestplot(mixed_fit) +
  add_forest_table()
```

Mixed-model plots show fixed effects, not random-effect variances or individual
cluster effects. P-values are shown only when supplied by the tidier.

## Compare fitted models

`bind_forest_models()` checks compatible effect scales, axis transformations,
reference values, and confidence levels. Labels follow the supplied model
order. Also check that outcomes, predictor units, and populations make the
comparison meaningful.

```{r bind-models, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5, dpi=300}
fit1 <- lm(mpg ~ cyl, data = mtcars)
fit2 <- lm(mpg ~ cyl + qsec, data = mtcars)
fit3 <- lm(mpg ~ cyl + qsec + wt, data = mtcars)

bound_models <- bind_forest_models(
  list(fit1, fit2, fit3),
  model_labels = c("Unadjusted", "Adjusted", "Fully Adjusted")
)

ggforestplot(bound_models, striped_rows = TRUE, p.value = "p.value") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-6, 2)) +
  theme(legend.position = "top") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#1F968BFF", "#453781FF", "#FDE725FF")) +
  add_forest_table(
    columns = c("term", "model", "estimate", "p.value"),
    p_digits = 4
  )
```


## Derive subgroup effects from an interaction model

For a fitted model with one continuous-by-factor interaction,
`subgroup = "auto"` identifies the factor from model metadata and estimates the
focal variable's average slope within each observed factor level.

```{r model-subgroup-effects}
interaction_fit <- lm(wt ~ hp + mpg * factor(cyl) + qsec, data = mtcars)

subgroup_ready <- tidy_forest_model(
  interaction_fit,
  subgroup = "auto",
  focal = "mpg"
)

as.data.frame(subgroup_ready)[, c(
  "term", "subgroup", "estimate", "conf.low", "conf.high", "p.value"
)]

ggforestplot(subgroup_ready, striped_rows = TRUE) +
  add_forest_table(columns = c("term", "estimate", "p"))
```

These rows are average `mpg` slopes within the `cyl` levels. They come from
`marginaleffects::avg_slopes()` using the original model and its covariance
matrix. No subgroup-specific models are refitted. The focal main effect, factor
main-effect coefficients, and raw interaction coefficients are replaced by the
derived block; unrelated coefficients remain standalone in formula order.

The same interaction can be selected explicitly:

```{r explicit-model-subgroup-effects}
tidy_forest_model(
  interaction_fit,
  subgroup = "cyl",
  focal = "mpg"
)
```

Automatic selection currently requires exactly one unambiguous
continuous-by-factor interaction. Factor-by-factor effects require explicit
predictor names and use `marginaleffects::avg_comparisons()`. Continuous
subgroups, transformed focal terms, multiple selected interactions, and
three-way interactions are rejected. Logistic and Cox effects are calculated
on their model scale and shown as odds ratios and hazard ratios by default, not
as marginal probabilities or survival probabilities.

The canonical `p.value` combines two compatible display roles: ordinary
covariates retain their coefficient p-values, while every derived subgroup
block receives an omnibus Wald test of the selected interaction. The display
layer moves that interaction p-value to the subgroup header and leaves the
individual levels blank, so one table column can present both kinds of tests.

Use `p_method = "level"` when the subgroup-specific slope or comparison tests
are the quantities that should appear beside the individual estimates:

```{r model-subgroup-level-p-values}
level_p_ready <- tidy_forest_model(
  interaction_fit,
  subgroup = "auto",
  focal = "mpg",
  p_method = "level"
)

ggforestplot(level_p_ready, striped_rows = TRUE) +
  add_forest_table(columns = c("term", "estimate", "p"))
```

Both methods use the same canonical `p.value` column. `"overall"` changes the
test and places it on the subgroup header; `"level"` retains the tests returned
for the derived effects and places them on the subgroup rows.

### Categorical-by-categorical
```{r subgroup-categorical}
fit2 <- lm(wt ~ as.factor(gear)*as.factor(cyl) + hp + am, data = mtcars)

fit2 |>
  tidy_forest_model(subgroup = "gear", focal = "cyl", p_method = "level") |>
  ggforestplot(striped_rows = TRUE) +
  theme(legend.position = "top") +
  add_forest_table(columns = c("term", "estimate", "p.value"))
```


For mixed models, derived effects are population-level (random effects set to
zero). Supported subgroup links are identity, logit, and log; Cox effects use
the linear-predictor scale.
